sap_vs_psf_depth: PSF (FLUX) box depth 2325 +- 123 ppm; SAP_FLUX box depth 1170 +- 78 ppm at the same ephemeris with the same transit-masked running-median detrend; ratio SAP/PSF = 0.50 +- 0.04. Raw per-quarter medians show the KBONUS SAP aperture (3-5 px, season dependent) holds 1.0-2.4x the PSF flux, so a dip on the target is expected to appear in SAP at FLFRCSAP*F_psf/F_sap = 0.41-0.88 of the PSF depth (median 0.55). Per season the measured ratio is 0.76+-0.10 (Q4/8/12/16, 3 px), 0.53+-0.09 (Q1/5/9/13/17), 0.39+-0.06 (Q2/6/10/14), 0.46+-0.05 (Q3/7/11/15, 5 px) against expected 0.86/0.60/0.43/0.41: chi2 = 3.1 for 4 seasons. A constant ratio gives chi2 = 10.3 and the CROWDSAP header keywords (0.83-0.97) give chi2 = 139. So the SAP depth is diluted exactly as the target's actual flux fraction in the aperture predicts, i.e. consistent with the dip being on the target (or within ~1 px of it); the CROWDSAP/crowdsap values in the headers and target CSV do not describe the real aperture contamination and would predict a SAP depth ~1.8x larger than observed. This test cannot separate the target from a sub-pixel neighbour; pixel-level localisation remains the decisive step.
disagreements: Box duration: my refined BLS gives 5.04 h, the pipeline 5.625 h; in my runs the box duration moves between 5.0 and 5.8 h depending on the period/duration grid because the event is a trapezoid (my fit: T14 = 6.35 +- 0.22 h, T23 = 4.43 h, T23/T14 = 0.70, uncorrected for 30-min cadence smearing; ~5.9 h after subtracting one cadence). The pipeline's t14_max for Rstar = 0.79 Rsun is 5.43 h, so my T14 implies a duration ratio of ~1.08-1.17 rather than the pipeline's 1.04: mild tension with a compact K-dwarf host, not a kill (Rstar is a photometric estimate; eccentricity or a larger host would also do it).
Empirical SNR: 18.9 (mine, random-phase MAD error 123 ppm) vs 20.6 (pipeline pass-2, box noise 109 ppm) and 22.0 (stage-1). Different error definitions; same conclusion.

Depth: 2325 +- 123 ppm (mine, 5.04-h box, masked re-detrend) vs 2242 +- 90 ppm (pipeline pass 2): 0.5 sigma apart; the offset is the box width (a 5.47-h box on my flux gives 2244 ppm). Per-event weighted mean 2319 +- 73 (mine) vs 2205 (pipeline); trapezoid depth 2353 +- 85.

Number of transits: 35 epochs with >= 50% in-transit coverage (mine) vs 36 (pipeline); the pipeline counts epoch 21 (BKJD 936.96) which has 5 of 11 expected cadences and sits 0.02 d from a gap edge. 36 epochs have any in-transit data; 39 fall within the baseline.

Per-event scatter: chi2/dof = 55.5/34 (1.63) in mine vs 70.9/35 (2.0) in the pipeline; both show mild excess. Epochs 6, 10 and 32 (BKJD 385, 533, 1341) are at 30-45% of the mean depth in both analyses; epoch 4 (BKJD 312) is high at +2.6 sigma and epoch 32 low at -2.8 sigma in mine. Every covered event is individually positive.

Inverted-flux null: my unmasked 1-d running-median detrend leaves +400 to +700 ppm shoulders 3-9 h either side of the transit, so the inverted flux (2 - f) shows a peak at the same period (SDE 14.2, phase offset -6.2 h, 648 ppm, 5.8 h) that vanishes after transit-masked re-detrending. The pipeline's inverted top peak is 0.855 d at SDE 16.2 instead. Not a disagreement about the signal, but a warning that inverted-null SDEs of ~15 can appear at the true period from detrending artefacts, and that the first-screen inverted null is only clean when the real signal is far above that level (here 71-78).

Season dependence of the PSF depth: Q4/8/12/16 (3-px aperture season, PSFFRAC 0.71) give 1895 +- 162 ppm vs ~2500 +- 230 ppm in Q2/6/10/14 and Q3/7/11/15 (~2 sigma); per-year depths are consistent, and the pipeline's quartile 1 is its highest rather than lowest. Noise-level, flagged only.

Header/CSV crowding metadata: CROWDSAP 0.83-0.97 and the target CSV crowdsap 0.83 are inconsistent with the raw fluxes (SAP aperture holds 1.0-2.4x the PSF flux per quarter). Any dilution argument built on those keywords is wrong for this star; the measured SAP/PSF depth ratio (0.50) is 8 sigma below what the keywords predict but matches FLFRCSAP*F_psf/F_sap in every season.

# Independent re-derivation: kic-010213563 (Gaia DR3 2128591018876020864)

Run: `runs/poolA_main/adversarial/kic-010213563/rederive/` (own code: `rederive_kic010213563.py`, `extra_checks.py`, `sap_by_season.py`; numbers in `results.json`, `extra.json`, `sap_by_season.json`). No code under `pipeline/` was imported or read; `vet.json`, `pixel.json` and `survivors.csv` were read only after `results.json` was final. Candidate language throughout: this is a transit-like **signal**, nothing more.

## Method (all from scratch, numpy/astropy only)
- Cached KBONUS-BKG stitched light curve, `SAP_QUALITY == 0`, finite: 59,999 cadences, 17 quarters, baseline 1459.5 d. Per-quarter median normalisation.
- Detrend: time-windowed running median (1.0 d), segments split at gaps > 0.5 d, asymmetric clipping (upper 3.5 MAD, lower 8 MAD). Second pass with the transit masked (|phase| < 0.75 dur) before any depth is measured. Flattened PSF-flux scatter 1370 ppm per cadence.
- Blind search: astropy `BoxLeastSquares`, likelihood objective, 1-50 d, my own log-uniform frequency grid (dlnf = 0.05 d / (3 x baseline); 342,574 trial periods), durations 1.2-7.9 h. The identical grid was run on the inverted flux (2 - f).
- Depth: box statistic mean(1-3 dur) - mean(|phase| < dur/2); error = robust std of 3000 random-phase boxes that avoid the transit and phase 0.5 (so red noise at the transit timescale is included).

## 1. Blind recovery (statistic: BLS SDE on the PSF flux, full 1-50 d grid)
| rank | period (d) | SDE (median-detrended) | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 36.76774 | 78.3 (raw SDE 70.7) | = pipeline 36.7671 (ratio 1/1) |
| 2 | 18.38355 | 33.6 | P/2 alias |
| 3 | 7.35342 | 18.0 | P/5 alias |

Inverted-flux null on the same grid: top SDE 14.2 at 36.7665 d and 14.2 at 1.710 d. The same-period inverted peak is a detrending artefact of my unmasked running median (shoulders of +400 to +700 ppm at 3-9 h from mid-transit; the inverted box sits 6.2 h off the transit and disappears after transit-masked re-detrending). Real/inverted SDE contrast: 71-78 vs 14.

## 2. Ephemeris and depth at the top peak (transit-masked re-detrend, PSF flux)
- P = 36.767192 d, t0 = BKJD 164.85097 (BJD 2454997.85097), 4.5 min from the pipeline's t0.
- BLS box duration 5.04 h (grid-dependent, 5.0-5.8 h across my runs). Trapezoid fit within +-1 d: depth 2353 +- 85 ppm, **T14 = 6.35 +- 0.22 h**, T23 = 4.43 h, T23/T14 = 0.70 (30-min smearing not removed; ~5.9 h corrected). Trapezoid beats a pure V by delta-chi2 = 34 and a pure box by 48 over 3178 points: U-shaped, flat-bottomed.
- **Box depth 2325 +- 123 ppm** (random-phase MAD; std 128), 343 in-transit cadences, **empirical SNR 18.9**. Per-event weighted mean 2319 +- 73 ppm. With an unmasked 1-d running median the depth is suppressed to 2107 ppm (the pipeline's stage-1 value of 1970 ppm has the same cause).
- Odd/even: 2349 +- 101 vs 2287 +- 105 ppm, **0.42 sigma** (box version 0.61 sigma).
- Secondary at phase 0.5: **-225 ppm (-1.82 sigma)**, i.e. a non-significant brightening, no eclipse.
- Per Kepler year (Q1-4, Q5-8, Q9-12, Q13-17): 2549 +- 296, 2189 +- 203, 2332 +- 191, 2268 +- 174 ppm. Consistent.
- Transits: 39 epochs in the baseline, 36 with any data, **35 with >= 50% coverage**; every covered event is positive; per-event chi2/dof = 55.5/34 (two |z| > 2.5 events: epoch 4 high, epoch 32 low).

## 3. SAP vs PSF flux (dilution)
SAP box depth 1170 +- 78 ppm, ratio SAP/PSF = 0.50 +- 0.04. The SAP aperture holds 1.0-2.4x the PSF flux depending on season, so the on-target expectation is FLFRCSAP x F_psf/F_sap = 0.41-0.88. Per season the measured ratio tracks that expectation (chi2 = 3.1 for 4 seasons: 0.76/0.53/0.39/0.46 measured vs 0.86/0.60/0.43/0.41 expected); a constant ratio gives chi2 = 10.3 and the CROWDSAP keywords give chi2 = 139. The dilution behaves as expected for a dip on (or within ~1 px of) the target. The CROWDSAP/crowdsap metadata (0.83-0.97) do not describe the real aperture and should not be used for this star.

## 4. Comparison with the pipeline (vet.json / survivors.csv)
| quantity | mine | pipeline |
|---|---|---|
| period (d) | 36.76719 (blind top 36.76774) | 36.76708 (screen 36.76630) |
| depth (ppm) | 2325 +- 123 box; 2319 +- 73 per-event; 2353 +- 85 trapezoid | 2242 +- 90 pass 2; 2205 event-weighted |
| duration (h) | 5.04 box; T14 6.35, T23 4.43 | 5.625 box (screen 4.5) |
| BLS SDE | 70.7 raw / 78.3 detrended | 73.9 |
| empirical SNR | 18.9 | 20.6 (screen 22.0) |
| odd/even | 0.42 sigma | 0.70 sigma |
| secondary | -225 ppm, -1.8 sigma | -171 ppm, -1.6 sigma |
| transits | 35 (36 with any data) | 36 |
| event chi2 | 55.5/34 | 70.9/35 |
| inverted null top SDE | 14.2 (36.77 d artefact) | 16.2 (0.855 d) |

**Verdict: the pipeline's period, depth, duration, odd/even, secondary and transit count are reproduced within errors by independent code; the signal is recovered blind as the top peak of a 1-50 d search with its P/2 and P/5 aliases as the next two peaks.** The disagreements listed are small and explained (box width, error definition, event-coverage cut, detrending shoulders). Two points for the red-team: (i) my trapezoid T14 of ~5.9-6.35 h is 8-17% longer than the maximum central-transit duration for the assumed 0.79 Rsun host (5.43 h), which is mild tension with a compact K-dwarf host or a hint of eccentricity/different host; (ii) three of 36 events are at 30-45% of the mean depth in both analyses, within the expected red-noise scatter but worth a look in the pixel data. Nothing here promotes the signal beyond what stage 2 and pixel localisation already support; TRICERATOPS and the known-object/novelty checks are still required before the word "candidate" is used.
